linux.fallback: constrained: the agent runs unprivileged, so other users' homes (usually 0700) are refused, not empty, and the listing is constrained; configured access as written, not sshd's effective policy (Match is not evaluated); CA trust, key and principals commands, a principals file, hostbased auth and AuthenticationMethods are not read; key comments, option values and key-file paths are never emitted; only homes under /home and /root are walked; a symlinked key file or .ssh is refused; network mounts are skipped
linux.mechanism: bounded reads of /etc/ssh/sshd_config (Include followed, config symlinks followed as sshd does) and each account's authorized_keys (no-follow; pure parsers, SHA-256 fingerprints); one bounded systemctl is-enabled argv per sshd unit

macos.fallback: configured access as written, not sshd's effective policy; the launchd override is not 'running'; CA trust, key and principals commands, a principals file, hostbased auth and AuthenticationMethods are not read; the Remote Login access list (pam_sacl) is not read; key comments, option values and key-file paths are never emitted; only homes under /Users owned by uid 500 or above, and /var/root, are walked; a symlinked key file or .ssh is refused; network mounts are skipped
macos.mechanism: bounded reads of /etc/ssh/sshd_config (Include followed, config symlinks followed as sshd does) and each account's authorized_keys (no-follow; pure parsers, SHA-256 fingerprints); one bounded launchctl print-disabled system argv

windows.fallback: not read yet: one unsupported status row, windows:planned

caveats: **Configured, not effective.** Rows report what the files say, not what `sshd` enforces: a `Match` block (including `Match all`) is counted and not evaluated, defaults are not applied (an unset setting is `-`), an `Include` wildcard is expanded in byte order where `sshd` uses locale order, and directives `sshd` would refuse are listed as written with only an unbalanced quote flagged. On macOS, Remote Login is also gated by an access list outside both files (`pam_sacl`, group `com.apple.access_ssh`), which a user can fail even with a key present and which this plugin does not read; `sshd -t` and `sshd -T` are the validity and effective-policy checks.

**A syntactic inventory, not `sshd`'s validity check.** A key row means the line parses by `sshd`'s grammar and its blob decodes completely, but option values are not validated, an ECDSA point is not checked against the curve, and a certificate's signature is not verified. A line of a key type this plugin does not know (`ssh-dss`, a newer algorithm) is counted malformed and never reported as a key, so a key `sshd` accepts can be missing here and a tampered certificate `sshd` rejects can appear; a certificate row reports the embedded key's fingerprint, not the certificate's.

**Identity is the home directory's name, and only these homes are walked.** `account` is the basename of the walked home, not the login name; Linux walks every directory directly under `/home` plus `/root`, macOS every `/Users` entry owned by uid 500 or above plus `/var/root`, so a service account with its home elsewhere is never seen and the plugin cannot tell it from an absent account. Over 512 homes the first 512 in directory order are kept (`homes:too_many`), any directory under a walked root such as `lost+found` is listed as an account, and an `AuthorizedKeysFile` entry using `%u`, `%U` or another token is reported unsupported rather than guessed.

**Blocking I/O on mounts is guarded by name, with residuals.** The config path, `Include` files, home roots, homes and key paths on a network filesystem named by the run-start mount table (`yuzu::shared::is_network_fstype`, plus `webdav`/`afpfs`/`macfuse`/`osxfuse` on macOS) are never opened, because an open on a dead hard mount pins a worker with no deadline. A stacked filesystem, a bare `fuse` mount over a dead server, a mount made after the snapshot, a link chain and an entry of a listed `Include` directory that is itself a link into a mount are not caught (#4875), and the reads carry no deadline of their own, so the worst case is 1,024 key-file reads of up to 1 MiB on one shared command worker.

**Windows is not read.** The Windows leg reports one `unsupported` row, `windows:planned`, and reads no key file, `sshd_config` or service state; the intended mechanism is a per-profile `.ssh\authorized_keys`, `%ProgramData%\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys` and `sshd_config` read through the profile walk. No leg runs `sshd -T`, so configured access is all this plugin reports on any OS.

definitions.description: The SSH public keys this host trusts through each account's authorized_keys, plus the sshd_config values that govern inbound access, as configured (read as written, Include followed, first occurrence wins; Match blocks are counted and not evaluated, including Match all, whose directives override the global values under sshd; defaults are not applied, so this is configured access and not sshd's effective policy; a directive or value sshd would refuse is skipped or listed as written with no token, and only an unbalanced quote is flagged: sshd -t is the validity check). It reports a SHA-256 fingerprint for every public key in the authorized_keys of the homes it walks (a certificate reports the fingerprint of the key it carries) with the option names it uses, and whether the sshd service is enabled. A login that needs no key is governed by the config rows: password, keyboard-interactive and GSSAPI are reported as written; other no-key methods (KerberosAuthentication, a PAM-supplied method) are not read. It does not read every way to log in: a certificate authority, keys or principals supplied by a command, a principals file, host-based authentication and AuthenticationMethods are not read (when sshd_config sets one of these six at global scope to a value other than its inert one the status is constrained, with a presence-only token). Two more gaps raise no token and are documented only: macOS Remote Login's access list is not read, and only homes under /home and /root (Linux) or under /Users owned by uid 500 or above and /var/root (macOS) are walked, so an account with its home elsewhere is not listed. Key comments, option values, principals and key-file paths are never emitted; the account is the home directory's name. A home or file the agent cannot read is reported as refused with a reason token (on Linux an unprivileged agent usually cannot open other users' homes, so constrained is the common outcome), never as an empty result. A line whose key type this plugin does not know is counted as malformed and never reported as a key (its blob cannot be decoded completely). Reads one machine per request and is off until enabled. The Windows leg is planned and not yet read. The first row is a status row stating whether the read was complete; if a leg threw after its rows had started, a second unsupported status row follows and is the one that counts.

description: SSH inbound-access audit: sshd_config as written, per-account authorized_keys fingerprints, sshd service state; never key comments, option values or paths
how_it_works:
`list` reports who can log in to this host over SSH, as configured, and changes nothing. It reads, in this order: `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` (with `Include` files followed at the directive's position), the state of the `sshd` service units, and the `authorized_keys` files of each account home it walks. It answers with a `status` row first saying whether the read was complete, then three `source` rows (`sshd_config`, `homes`, `service`, each `read`, `absent`, `refused` or `failed`, so zero `key` rows is never an ambiguous empty success), a `config` row for every allowlisted setting, the `service` rows, and one `file` row per `authorized_keys` file followed by a `key` row for every key line `sshd` would accept. A leg that throws after its rows have started adds a second `unsupported` status row, which wins.

`sshd_config` is read as `sshd` reads it: the first value of a setting wins, and a `Match` block is counted but never evaluated. A key row carries the type, the fingerprint (byte-identical to `ssh-keygen -lf`; a certificate reports the key it carries) and the option **names** it uses; every key blob is decoded completely and within bounds. A key comment, an option **value** and any key-file path are never emitted (see Sensitivity). The plugin is deliberately a configured-access inventory, not `sshd -T`, not a login history and not a validity check.

**What it does not read.** `sshd` can accept a login from sources this plugin never opens: a certificate authority (`TrustedUserCAKeys`), keys or principals supplied by a command (`AuthorizedKeysCommand`, `AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand`), a principals file (`AuthorizedPrincipalsFile`), host-based authentication (`HostbasedAuthentication yes`) and a method requirement that changes what a key alone is worth (`AuthenticationMethods`). When `sshd_config` sets one of those sources at global scope to a value other than its inert one (`none`; `no` for `HostbasedAuthentication`; `any` for `AuthenticationMethods`; see the `CONSTRAINED` row below) the listing is `CONSTRAINED` with `<os>:remote_access_audit:sshd_config:other_credential_sources`: the token is presence only (no value, no path), and it means the key rows are not the whole answer to who can log in. The same holds for the Remote Login access list on macOS (caveat 1) and for any account whose home is outside the walked roots (caveat 3). A login that needs no key is governed by the `config` rows: the no-key methods reported are password, keyboard-interactive and GSSAPI (`passwordauthentication`, `kbdinteractiveauthentication`, `gssapiauthentication`), as written and never flagged; other no-key methods (`KerberosAuthentication`, a PAM-supplied method) are not read.

**Symlinks follow a two-tier rule.** Under `/etc/ssh` (writable by root only: `sshd_config`, the `Include` directory, each `Include` file) a link is followed as `sshd` follows it, so stock macOS and NixOS links do not make the listing `CONSTRAINED`; a target outside `/etc/ssh` is read with no owner or mode check (`sshd` applies none), and a non-regular target is still refused. A home parent (`/home`, `/Users`) is root-owned too, so one link hop is allowed (Fedora Atomic ships `/home -> var/home`). Where the audited account can write (a home, `.ssh`, `authorized_keys*`, an absolute `AuthorizedKeysFile` path) a link is never followed, because a root agent would read what the account cannot: that file reports `failed` with a `symlink_refused` or `enotdir` token. Absolute paths and homes are opened from `/` one component at a time without following a link, so a link anywhere in the chain is refused; the macOS root home is therefore configured as `/private/var/root`, the canonical spelling of `/var/root`.
name: remote_access_audit

columns.description: Row shape discriminator (field 0). Values: status, source, config, service, file, key.
columns.name: row_kind

columns.description: status: the literal "list". source: sshd_config, homes or service. config: the setting (permitrootlogin, passwordauthentication, pubkeyauthentication, kbdinteractiveauthentication, gssapiauthentication, permitemptypasswords, usepam, port, authorizedkeysfile, allowusers_count, allowgroups_count, denyusers_count, denygroups_count, match_blocks). service: the unit (ssh.service, sshd.service, ssh.socket, sshd.socket, or com.openssh.sshd on macOS). file and key: the account, which is the HOME DIRECTORY NAME, not necessarily the login name.
columns.name: field_1

columns.description: status: supported, constrained, permission_denied or unsupported (the planned Windows leg, and a leg that threw). source: read, absent, refused or failed (absent is a state, not a failure). config: the value as written in the first occurrence, "-" when unset or sshd_config was not read; authorizedkeysfile reports only default, none or custom:<n>, never a path; the counts are numbers. service: the state - systemctl is-enabled output (enabled, enabled-runtime, linked, linked-runtime, alias, masked, masked-runtime, static, indirect, disabled, generated, transient, bad, not-found) or enabled/disabled for launchd, or unknown (never read as disabled). file: authorized_keys, authorized_keys2 or custom. key: the same kind.
columns.name: field_2

columns.description: status: reason token(s) for a non-supported read, "-" when complete; tokens look like linux:remote_access_audit:homes:permission_denied or windows:planned. source: files read (sshd_config plus includes), accounts walked, or units queried, "-" unless read. config: where the value came from (sshd_config or include:<file name>), "-" when unset. service: the mechanism. file: read, absent, refused or failed. key: the key type as written (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa, ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, a -cert-v01 certificate type, ...).
columns.name: field_3

columns.description: source (homes row only): the number of home-root entries not treated as accounts (macOS: owned by a uid under 500, such as /Users/Shared), "-" on Linux where nothing is detectably skipped, or when the roots were not listed (counted over the homes examined: a lower bound when keys:row_cap, keys:file_cap or homes:too_many is set). file: the number of key lines listed (accepted and within the row budget; keys:row_cap in the status reason means the listing stopped before the last accepted line of the file), "-" unless read. key: the fingerprint, SHA256: plus unpadded base64, identical to ssh-keygen -lf (a certificate reports the key it carries).
columns.name: field_4

columns.description: file: the number of lines sshd would not accept (unparseable key, unknown option, unknown key type, a truncated or trailing-byte blob, a certificate signature that is truncated or has trailing bytes, RSA under 1024 bits), "-" unless read. key: the key size in bits (RSA modulus, 256 for ed25519, the curve size for ECDSA).
columns.name: field_5

columns.description: file: the number of lines over 16 KiB that were not parsed, "-" unless read. key: comma-separated flags from cert_authority, certificate, has_command, has_from, has_principals, or "-".
columns.name: field_6

columns.description: key: the lowercased option NAMES the line carries (restrict, cert-authority, [no-]port-forwarding, [no-]agent-forwarding, [no-]x11-forwarding, [no-]touch-required, [no-]verify-required, [no-]pty, [no-]user-rc, command, principals, from, expiry-time, environment, permitopen, permitlisten, tunnel), or "-". Option VALUES are never emitted. Not used by the other kinds.
columns.name: field_7

outputs_note: Every row is pipe-delimited; field 0 is the row kind and `-` is an absent value; the order and the field meanings are in the table below. `port` is comma-joined across occurrences, and the deprecated `ChallengeResponseAuthentication` shares the `kbdinteractiveauthentication` slot. `unknown` in a `service` row means two things: on Linux it always comes with a `service:*` or `subprocess_runner:*` token and a `CONSTRAINED` listing (the unit could not be queried); on macOS the read succeeded and launchd has no override entry for the label, so the status stays `supported` (`enabled` there is a launchd override, not "running"). Every free field is scrubbed of NUL and invalid UTF-8, pipe-escaped and cut at 4096 bytes.

privileges.grant: None for `launchctl print-disabled system`, which answers an unprivileged caller. Reading another user's `~/.ssh` needs the access the agent identity already has as root; an identity that cannot open a home reports it refused. Homes walked: the entries of `/Users` owned by uid 500 or above, and `/var/root` (the rest are counted on the `homes` source row, not read)
privileges.if_refused: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `macos:remote_access_audit:<source>:permission_denied` when a source was refused and none was read, `CONSTRAINED` when another source was read; the `file` row says `refused`
privileges.measured: `launchctl print-disabled system` and `/etc/ssh` reads verified as a normal user on macOS 26.6.2; see Sample output

privileges.grant: None for `systemctl is-enabled`. Homes walked: every directory directly under `/home`, and `/root`. `sshd_config` is world-readable (0644) on the Debian-family packages but **0600 root on the RHEL family** (verified on Rocky 9 and Amazon Linux 2023), where the unprivileged agent reads it as `refused` with `linux:remote_access_audit:sshd_config:permission_denied`. **Other users' homes are usually 0700 or 0750, so an unprivileged agent cannot open them: `CONSTRAINED` with `linux:remote_access_audit:homes:permission_denied` and one `refused` file row per `AuthorizedKeysFile` entry per account (two by default) is the common outcome, never "no keys".** The real options are accepting the refusal or granting the agent `CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH` as an **ambient** capability: a systemd drop-in for the agent unit (`[Service]` `AmbientCapabilities=CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH`). A file capability on the agent binary does not work on the packaged unit, because `NoNewPrivileges=true` (`deploy/systemd/yuzu-agent.service`) makes file capabilities inert (verified in a container: effective capabilities empty under it, present with ambient capabilities). The trade-off is real: `CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH` lets every plugin the agent hosts read any file the agent can name, so grant it only where this audit is wanted. Packaging for it is #4916; do not loosen home modes
privileges.if_refused: `PERMISSION_DENIED` / partial with `linux:remote_access_audit:<source>:permission_denied` when a source was refused and none was read, `CONSTRAINED` when another source was read
privileges.measured: Not measured on the `yuzu-agent` account; the capture runs as euid 0 in a container, see Sample output
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, dedicated unprivileged account (`yuzu-agent` on the packaged unit), never root by design (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: every source that exists was read in full; no keys is `supported` with `file` rows saying `absent` or `read|0`

result_status.provenance: `<os>:remote_access_audit:sshd_config:<cause>`, `<os>:remote_access_audit:include:<cause>`, `<os>:remote_access_audit:keys:<cause>`, with `<cause>` one of `symlink_refused`, `not_regular`, `oversized`, `invalid_bytes`, `invalid_quotes` (`sshd_config` only: a configuration line in that file or an `Include` file with an unterminated quote, skipped as `sshd` would refuse it), or an errno token (`eio`, `eloop`, `enotdir`, `enametoolong`, `errno_<n>`); the same causes appear on `homes` (`<os>:remote_access_audit:homes:<errno token>`, a home root or home that could not be listed or opened; when only some home roots could not be listed, the homes that did list are still audited and the `homes` source row keeps its error state (`refused` or `failed`) with `-` counts)
result_status.when: a file could not be read: a symlinked key-side file, `.ssh` or home (not followed: the `file` row is `failed` with `symlink_refused`), a dangling link among the entries of a listed `Include` directory (`include:enoent`: the directory listed the name and it then reads absent; a literal `Include` path that reads absent is silent, as an `Include` wildcard that matches nothing is in `sshd`) or a loop (`include:eloop`), a FIFO or other non-regular target, a file over 256 KiB (config) or 1 MiB (keys), a NUL byte in `sshd_config` or an `Include` file (in `authorized_keys` a NUL cuts that line only, see the keys row below), an I/O error; its source or `file` row says `failed` and the other sources are still reported

an `Include` was not followed: nested deeper than 4 levels, more than 32 `Include` patterns (arguments) or included files in all (every pattern counts, even one whose wildcard matches nothing, and a single `Include` line with 33 patterns is over the cap), inside a `Match` block (whose condition is not evaluated), or a `~` path or wildcard in a directory component

an `AuthorizedKeysFile` entry uses `%u`, `%U`, another token or `~` and was skipped (never guessed), or `AuthorizedKeysFile` also appears inside a `Match` block (the global value is used), or it lists more than 100 paths (the first 100 are read, the `authorizedkeysfile` row still reports the real count)

`sshd_config` sets, at global scope, a keyword for a login source this plugin does not read to a value other than its inert one (`none`; `no` for `HostbasedAuthentication`; `any` for `AuthenticationMethods`): `TrustedUserCAKeys`, `AuthorizedKeysCommand`, `AuthorizedPrincipalsFile`, `AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand`, `HostbasedAuthentication yes` or an `AuthenticationMethods` other than `any`. `GSSAPIAuthentication` is not in this set: it is a `config` row. Presence only: no value and no path is emitted, and the first occurrence decides (a first `none` leaves a later value ignored, as in `sshd`); a `Match`-scoped directive is counted by `match_blocks` and not flagged

an `authorized_keys` line `sshd` would not accept (unparseable key, unknown option, a second `command`/`from`/`principals`, truncated or trailing-byte blob or certificate signature, RSA under 1024 bits) or a line over 16 KiB was counted and not emitted; or a line of a key type this plugin does not know was refused and counted malformed (it is not reported as a key); or a line held a NUL byte and was read only up to it, as `sshd` reads it (the file row stays `read` and the key before the NUL is reported)

the `sshd_config` file, an `Include` file or directory, a home root, home or key path on a network filesystem named by the run-start mount table was never opened; or the mount table could not be read (nothing is guarded, the config half included); or more than 512 accounts, 1024 key-file reads or 2048 rows / 1 MiB were reached (the listing stops there; when a single `authorized_keys` file is what fills the row budget its `file` row and its first keys are kept and the rest, including later accounts, are not listed); or a directory held more than 4096 entries (only the first 4096 are examined, `homes:too_many` or `include:too_many`); or a field was cut at 4096 bytes

the service query failed: the tool is not installed or could not be started (a non-systemd host: `systemctl_unavailable`/`launchctl_unavailable`, a failed service source and never "disabled"), timed out, was cut short, printed nothing or something unrecognised; the `service` source row says `failed` when no unit answered or any unit's query failed (the units that did answer keep their rows, and a failed unit's own row says `unknown`). A missing unit is not a failure: `systemd` 249 and 252 print `Failed to get unit file state for <unit>: No such file or directory` on stderr, which is read as `not-found`. `subprocess_runner:spawn_error` and `subprocess_runner:line_limit` are never emitted by this plugin: an unstartable tool is `service:*_unavailable`, and the runner is never told to stop at the line cap
a source was refused and no source was read; accumulated constrained tokens may follow, comma-joined
Windows: one `status|list|unsupported|windows:planned` row (caveat 5); or a leg threw, reported as an `unsupported` status row instead of unwinding across the plugin boundary

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the standard `ResponseStore`, kept 90 days (`--response-retention-days`, default 90) and served over `GET /api/responses` (legacy), `GET /api/v1/responses/{id}` and the equivalent MCP result-poll tools. `list` is also a gathered definition (`crossplatform.security.remote_access_audit`, 3600s TTL).
**Not consumed by** daily-sync, TAR, DEX, or metrics.

**Default off, and how to turn it on.** The plugin is Forensics-class and ships off: the server seeds a default-off kill switch at boot, so nothing dispatches until an operator runs `PUT /api/v1/plugin-config/remote_access_audit/kill-switch {"enabled":true}` (`PluginConfig:Write`, audited as `plugin_config.kill_switch.set`; the MCP twin is `set_plugin_kill_switch`). After that, dispatch is gated at `Forensics:Read` with `AdminOrApproval` (Administrator by default; a non-admin needs a delegated `Forensics:Read` grant plus an approval) and is single-target: exactly one device per request. While the switch is off, REST `/api/command` answers "permission denied: Forensics:Read" even to an Administrator, the dashboard console says "No agents connected", MCP returns an "emergency stop" message, and instruction execute answers 503 "no agents reached ... concurrency claim" (misleading; check the switch first). The switch is checked when a command is dispatched: disabling stops new dispatches, a run already in flight completes, and a delayed or staggered command already sent still runs (up to 10 minutes).

**Sensitivity.** Per-account key fingerprints on one named machine are identity material: they say which keys can log in as which account, and the account is the home directory's name. Key comments, option values, principals lists and key-file paths are never emitted. A key fingerprint is the same on every host that trusts the key, so results from two machines can be joined on it to show where one person's or one service's key is trusted: that cross-host linkability is inherent in the fact reported, and listing every walked home as an account, keyless ones included, is deliberate. Which accounts hold keys that can log in to a named machine is works-council co-determination-relevant. In the macOS sample the account name is replaced with `jsmith`. Dispatch is gated `Forensics:Read` + `AdminOrApproval`, but stored rows are readable by any `Response:Read` holder (Administrator, Operator, Viewer, PlatformEngineer and ITServiceOwner by default; any authenticated session while RBAC is off), audited as `response.read` on REST v1 `/responses/{id}`, `/aggregate` and `/export` and on the legacy `/api/responses/...` twins (all fail-closed), `execution.detail.fetch` (`/executions/{id}/responses`) and `mcp.query_responses`; the dashboard results view writes no audit row (known gap #4990). There is no per-user erasure path. The Instructions UAT runner cannot exercise Forensics-tier dispatch (known gap #5261); neither gap is fixed here.
**Siblings:** `privacy_permissions`, `browser_inventory` and `execution_artifacts` (the other Forensics-class plugins) and `mgmt_posture` (which plane controls the device).
